questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose U of T as it was an English speaking university and because it seemed to provide a unique academic opportunity for me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The biggest challenge was sifting through every mail to make sure that you did not miss an important link or piece of information. It could be helpful to simplify the entire process and reduce the number of emails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a 1 hour introduction talk which was quite good, everything considered. A nice woman helped me with an issue, I was having.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite hard to find a place to live in a city that you have never been. I stayed at Harrington housing on Sherbourne St. Unfortunately, I can't really recommend this place.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is hard to say. It is a large city and I expect every off-campus experience is different. Mine was not the best, but I would not want to generalise.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I felt that the assistance, I received, amounted to no more than being rejected for on-campus housing, and then being told: "Good luck". This is fair enough considering Toronto seems to be in somewhat of a housing crisis, but nevertheless it was bad news to say the least.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I found that the course selection proces was very disappointing. I did not receive any truly useful information, and I was rejected for a course for which I was entirely eligible. Only after I filed a complaint, the decision was overturned. 

As an exchange student, it is very easy to feel unimportant or overlooked in these situations and a blank rejection without valid reason was not the best introduction to the university. The rejection ultimately led me to being placed further back in the queue for the course, and thus ultimately to me not being able to take the course.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We were asked to fill out Google Forms-formulas with the course in question and the prove of eligibility given the required prerequisites.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We were giving an information sheet.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Almost entirely unsuccesful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have a good look at the prerequisites and be prepared to apply for a "backup" course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did two 300-level courses, one 200-level course and one 400-level course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I must admit, I prefer the Danish style of teaching. There is a very large use of PowerPoint (or similar) at U of T and it seemed that normal practice for students is to write notes directly on the slides using an iPad. I prefer that my professors use blackboard.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
CSC263 - Data Structure and Analysis
PHY407 - Computational Physics
PHY331 - Biological Physics
PHY392 - Climate Physics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: None of the above.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were too many to list. Check out the University's website, they have so many!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: They have 4 excellent gyms scattered around campus:)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit Niagara falls and plan a trip to Montreal.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy enough

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There were no particularly challenging cultural differences.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The architecture was quite nice. I found Robarts library to be super cozy.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Beware of prerequisites for courses.

Try to find a student co-op for housing. I wasn't able to myself, but some of my friends lived in one and that was amazing for them.

Good luck!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Scotty Bons makes wonderful jerk chicken. Huge recommendation! I ate there at least once a week:)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting wonderful people and simply overcoming the challenge of moving to a foreign country all by myself.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Moving to a foreign country all by myself.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
